body:
Thanks for the report @cazino!

IMHO we should get rid of the `finalize` method and instead just store the converted XML representation at that point, discarding the `_NodeReporter` instance, instead of keeping the instance around without any attributes.

after finalization the item should be removed from the mapping finalization needs to be reordered
this regression is my mistake - i expected the test for double id's to catch it

> after finalization the item should be removed from the mapping finalization needs to be reordered

I agree, but perhaps it would be simpler still to just get rid of `_NodeReporter.finalize()` at all? I mean, instead of:

``` python
    if report.when == "teardown":
        self.node_reporter(report).finalize()
```

We can just get the xml representation and save it separately, while discarding the reporter instance:

``` python
    if report.when == "teardown":
        reporter = self.node_reporter(report)
        self.xml_testsuites.append(reporter.to_xml())
        del self.node_reporters[reporter.key]
```

`xml_testsuites` would replace `node_reporters_ordered`, as there's no need to keep the node reporters sorted anymore, `xml_testsuites` will contain the xml snippets ready for dumping to the file during `pytest_sessionfinish`. 

Hope my explanation makes sense! :sweat_smile: 

> this regression is my mistake - i expected the test for double id's to catch it

No worries, it happens. :smile:

its missing a call to unicode(), we dont want to keep the xml tree

the main reason finalize clears things up so radically is to show bugs
in the long term i'd rather se py.test return to creating unique test ids per node

> its missing a call to unicode(), we dont want to keep the xml tree

`to_xml()` doesn't already return a `unicode`?
no, the finalize method makes the unicode as of now
As the bug is critical, I'll leave the patch to you guys.
the patch itself is small i think, the test is whats tricky

issue.title: CallInfo.__repr__ raises AttributeError if called before __init__ is finished

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: problem that needs to be addressed

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: easy issue that is friendly to new contributor

repository.name: pytest
repository.description: The pytest framework makes it easy to write small tests, yet scales to support complex functional testing

issue.body:
py.test version: 3.6.0
Python version: 3.6.4

The `result` attribute of `CallInfo` objects is assigned in `__init__` as the result of calling the test function. This means that `result` is only defined after the test function has finished executing.
If however, the test function extracts local variables from the stack (and does anything causing `__repr__` to be called on them) this causes an AttributeError since `CallInfo.__repr__` expects `result` to be defined.

Minimum example:
```python
import sys
from traceback import print_list, StackSummary, walk_stack


def print_stack():
    stack = StackSummary.extract(walk_stack(sys._getframe().f_back), capture_locals=True)
    stack.reverse()
    print_list(stack)


def test_bla():
    print_stack()
    # ^ This will crash with `AttributeError: 'CallInfo' object has no attribute 'result'`
    assert 1 == 1
```
